mainTopic: The קנס for forced relations: when קידושין takes effect, the נדה case, and whether death from Heaven exempts from payment
overview: The amud opens by finishing the search for the practical difference between two views on which women receive the קנס. One view asks whether קידושין can take effect, and the other asks whether he may keep her as a wife. Following רבי ישבב, the first answer is women forbidden only by a positive מצוה, such as an Egyptian or Edomite convert. The גמרא then says that if רבי ישבב's rule is broad, even those cases produce a ממזר. So it gives a new case instead: a בעולה with a כהן גדול, because that עשה does not apply to everyone. רב חסדא then teaches that everyone agrees a man who forced a נדה pays the קנס, since she passes both tests. Next, the גמרא notes that the משנה rejects רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, who held that anyone liable to death from Heaven is exempt from payment. אביי learns that view from the word אסון, which appears in two פסוקים. רב אדא בר אהבה challenges that proof, and the גמרא begins asking how to sort cold and heat, and lions and thieves, between harm from Heaven and harm from people. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The difference is women forbidden by a positive מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי ישבב's reading of רבי עקיבא, the difference between the two opinions is חייבי עשה, such as an Egyptian or Edomite convert.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is women forbidden by a positive מצוה, such as an Egyptian or Edomite convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to 'what is the difference between the two opinions?' It points to women who are forbidden only by a positive מצוה‎ (עשה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an Egyptian or Edomite convert, קידושין does take effect, so the child is not a ממזר. But he may not keep her as his wife. So one test (does קידושין take effect?) says yes, and the other test (may he stay married to her?) says no. That gap is the practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Women forbidden to him only by a positive מצוה
An Egyptian convert (first or second generation)
An Edomite convert (first or second generation)
The fixed fine paid for forcing or seducing a girl

phrases.english: Those forbidden by a positive מצוה: an Egyptian and an Edomite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to 'מאי בינייהו' that began on the previous amud (29b), following רבי ישבב's reading of רבי עקיבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference between the opinions is חייבי עשה, such as Egyptian or Edomite converts.

steps.title: If רבי ישבב states a broad rule, even positive-מצוה cases are included
steps.stepSummary: The answer works only if רבי ישבב is just arguing with רבי סימאי. If he is stating his own broad rule, even חייבי עשה would produce a ממזר, and then no difference is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי ישבב if he only comes to reject רבי סימאי's reasoning. But if he is stating his own rule, 'anyone who has no permitted relations among Jews, the child is a ממזר', then even women forbidden by a positive מצוה are included. So what is the difference between the opinions?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It asks how strongly to read רבי ישבב's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe רבי ישבב only meant to push back on רבי סימאי, who said only a widow with a כהן גדול is not a ממזר. If so, he may still agree that חייבי עשה are not ממזרים. But his actual words are broad: anyone forbidden to him. Read that way, even חייבי עשה produce a ממזר, so קידושין never takes effect there, and the difference from step 1 disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (the opening of a challenge)
To reject or exclude
His own reasoning, an independent rule
Permitted relations within the Jewish people
A child born from a union in which קידושין cannot take effect

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישבב is not giving his own halacha here. He is reporting, and protesting against, what he understands רבי עקיבא to hold.

phrases.english: This works well according to רבי ישבב
if it is to reject the reasoning of רבי סימאי
that he comes, then fine.
But if he is stating his own reasoning,
'anyone who has no permitted relations among Jews,
the child is a ממזר',
then even those forbidden by a positive מצוה are included!
phrases.notes: In other words, an Egyptian or Edomite convert would also produce a ממזר, so step 1's answer falls apart.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: Between the two תנאים in the earlier dispute, שמעון התימני and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב, אִי לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִטַּעְמָא דְּרַבִּי סִימַאי קָאָתֵי — שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 1's answer by reading רבי ישבב's statement as a broad, independent rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חייבי עשה is the practical difference according to רבי ישבב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישבב's words, 'anyone who has no permitted relations among Jews', cover חייבי עשה too. Then קידושין fails in those cases as well, and no case is left where the two tests give different results.

steps.title: The difference is a non-virgin with a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the difference is a בעולה (non-virgin) with a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a non-virgin with a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case where the two opinions still split: a כהן גדול with a woman who is not a virgin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here קידושין takes effect and the child is not a ממזר. But the כהן גדול may not keep her as his wife. So one test says she receives the קנס and the other says she does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is not a virgin
The High Priest, who must marry a virgin

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: a non-virgin with a כהן גדול.
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול is commanded to marry a virgin (ויקרא 21:13–14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2's challenge by offering a different practical-difference case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers a new case for the practical difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once חייבי עשה produce ממזרים, no case remains where the opinions differ.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בעולה with a כהן גדול is still a case where קידושין takes effect but he may not keep her, so the opinions split.

steps.title: Why is the כהן גדול case different from other positive מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the כהן גדול case should be treated differently from other חייבי עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 3. A בעולה with a כהן גדול is also forbidden by a positive מצוה, so why shouldn't רבי ישבב's broad rule cover it too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said that, according to רבי ישבב, even חייבי עשה produce a ממזר. The כהן גדול's duty to marry a virgin is also an עשה. So the גמרא needs a reason why this case falls outside the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is different? (asks for a distinction)

phrases.english: And what is different?
phrases.notes: Different from the Egyptian and Edomite case, which is also a positive מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 3's answer using the reasoning of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a בעולה with a כהן גדול is still a case where קידושין takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is also an עשה, and step 2 said רבי ישבב's rule covers חייבי עשה.

steps.title: This positive מצוה does not apply to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The duty to marry a virgin is an עשה that applies only to the כהן גדול. That makes it weaker, so even רבי ישבב's rule does not turn the child into a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a positive מצוה that does not apply equally to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the כהן גדול case is different: this מצוה applies only to the כהן גדול, not to all Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is lenient in two ways. It is only an עשה, not a לאו, and it applies to just one person, the כהן גדול. The Egyptian and Edomite rule, by contrast, applies to all Jews. So קידושין still takes effect here, but he may not keep her, and the two opinions split.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה that does not apply equally to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישבב, the practical difference between the opinions is a בעולה with a כהן גדול. קידושין takes effect, so the child is not a ממזר, but he may not keep her as his wife.

phrases.english: Because it is a positive מצוה
that does not apply equally to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ עֲשֵׂה שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by explaining why this עשה is weaker.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every עשה is treated the same way, so the כהן גדול case would also produce a ממזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: An עשה that applies only to the כהן גדול is weaker, so קידושין still takes effect.

steps.title: רב חסדא: everyone agrees one who forced a נדה pays the fine
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that everyone agrees a man who forced a נדה pays the קנס, because she passes both tests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Everyone agrees that one who forced a נדה pays the fine. According to the view that requires קידושין to take effect, here too קידושין takes effect. According to the view that requires her to be fit for him to keep as a wife, here too she is fit for him to keep.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא opens a new teaching. He names a case where every opinion agrees the קנס is paid: forced relations with a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with a נדה carry כרת, yet קידושין still takes effect with her, so she passes the first test. Her נדה status is only temporary, and he may marry her and stay with her, so she passes the second test as well. Since both tests agree, every opinion requires the קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her state of menstrual impurity
Everyone agrees
קידושין taking effect (from ולו תהיה לאשה)
Fit for him to keep as his wife

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that every כרת case means no קנס. With a נדה, the איסור of relations is serious, but קידושין still takes effect and she can stay married to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the test is about whether a marriage is possible, not about how serious the איסור of the act is.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
Everyone agrees about one who forced relations with a נדה
that he pays the fine.
According to the one who says the test is whether קידושין takes effect,
with this one too, קידושין takes effect.
According to the one who says the test is whether she is fit for him to keep,
this one too is fit for him to keep.
phrases.notes: Her נדה status ends, so he can stay married to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּבָא עַל הַנִּדָּה שֶׁמְּשַׁלֵּם קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching that uses the same two tests discussed above.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who forced a נדה pays the קנס according to every opinion, because קידושין takes effect with her and she is fit for him to keep.

steps.title: The משנה rejects רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's view
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's ruling that one who forces his sister pays a קנס excludes the view of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה. He treated יום הכפורים like שבת: someone who deserves death is exempt from payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rules out the view of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה. A ברייתא teaches that he treated יום הכפורים like שבת for payments. On שבת, a person who deserves death does not pay. In the same way, on יום הכפורים a person who deserves death does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה's ruling disagrees with רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, and it quotes his view from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a man who forces his sister pays the קנס, even though relations with a sister carry כרת. רבי נחוניא בן הקנה holds that כרת, which is death from Heaven, exempts a person from payment, just as death by בית דין does. He shows this by comparing יום הכפורים (כרת) to שבת (death by בית דין).

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude; to rule out another view
money payments
liable with his life; deserves death
the Day of Atonement, which carries כרת for breaking it

steps.confusionAlert: Breaking שבת on purpose brings death by בית דין, but breaking יום הכפורים brings כרת, which is death from Heaven. רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's new point is that the two are treated the same for payments.

phrases.english: And this comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה's ruling that a man who forces his sister still pays the קנס.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana
would make Yom Kippur
like Shabbat with regard to payments.
Just as on Shabbat, one who deserves death
is exempt from payment,
so too on Yom Kippur, one who deserves death
is exempt from payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: which earlier view the משנה's ruling rejects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה rejects רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, who exempts anyone liable to כרת from payment, comparing יום הכפורים to שבת.

steps.title: What is רבי נחוניא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason רבי נחוניא בן הקנה has for his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's view. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that death by בית דין exempts a person from payment. The question is how we know that death from Heaven (כרת) works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that death from Heaven also exempts a person from payment.

steps.title: אביי: the word אסון links both kinds of death
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the word אסון is used for death by people and also for death from Heaven. Since one exempts from payment, so does the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The word אסון is used for harm by people, and the word אסון is used for harm from Heaven. Just as harm by people exempts from payment, harm from Heaven also exempts from payment.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the source for רבי נחוניא בן הקנה by linking the same word in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמות, the word אסון refers to a killing that is punished by death, and that exempts from payment. In בראשית, יעקב uses אסון for harm that comes from Heaven. Because the same word appears in both places, אביי treats them the same, so death from Heaven also exempts from payment.

keyTerms.meaning: disaster; deadly harm
by the hands of people (for example, execution by בית דין)
by the hands of Heaven

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It says 'harm' about death at the hands of people.
And it says 'harm' about death at the hands of Heaven.
phrases.notes: בראשית 42:38. Here יעקב worries that harm might happen to בנימין on the way.

phrases.english: Just as the 'harm' stated about the hands of people
exempts from payment,
so too the 'harm' stated about the hands of Heaven
exempts from payment.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the same word אסון is used in both פסוקים, death from Heaven exempts from payment just like death by people.

steps.title: Maybe יעקב meant harm from people
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks how we know יעקב's אסון means harm from Heaven, like cold and heat. Maybe he meant lions and thieves, which are harm from people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה challenged this: How do you know that when יעקב warned his sons, he meant cold and heat, which come from Heaven? Maybe he meant lions and thieves, which come from people!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks אביי's source by questioning what kind of harm יעקב had in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's whole proof needs יעקב's אסון to mean harm from Heaven. If יעקב meant harm from people, then both פסוקים talk about the same kind of harm, and nothing is learned about death from Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged it strongly
cold and heat
a lion and thieves

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּאי דְּכִי קָא מַזְהַר לְהוּ יַעֲקֹב לִבְנֵיהּ,
phrases.english: From where do you know that when Jacob warned his sons,

phrases.aramaic: עַל צִינִּים וּפַחִים דְּבִידֵי שָׁמַיִם נִינְהוּ?
phrases.english: it was about cold and heat, which are at the hands of Heaven?
Perhaps it was about a lion and thieves,
which are at the hands of people?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reading of the פסוק in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that יעקב's אסון means harm from Heaven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If יעקב meant harm from people, the link between the two uses of אסון teaches nothing about death from Heaven.

steps.title: יעקב warned about every kind of danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that יעקב did not warn about only one kind of danger. He warned about all dangers, so his אסון includes harm from Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think יעקב warned about this kind and not about that kind? יעקב warned about everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by saying יעקב's warning covered every kind of danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worried father warns about every danger, not just one. So the word אסון in יעקב's words includes harm from Heaven too, and אביי's link between the פסוקים still works.

keyTerms.meaning: is it so that...? (asked in surprise)
he warned

phrases.english: Is that to say Jacob warned about this,
but did not warn about that?
Jacob warned about all matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא בר אהבה's challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadens the meaning of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעקב may have warned only about harm from people.
steps.terutzMaskana: יעקב warned about all harm, including harm from Heaven, so the proof stands.

steps.title: Are cold and heat really from Heaven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether cold and heat are really harm from Heaven. A ברייתא says everything is from Heaven except cold and heat, because a person can protect himself from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are cold and heat really from Heaven? A ברייתא teaches: Everything is in Heaven's hands except cold and heat, as it says: 'Cold and heat are on the path of the crooked; he who guards his soul will stay far from them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the assumption from step 10 that cold and heat count as harm from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says cold and heat are the one thing not left to Heaven, because a person who is careful can avoid them. So they seem to be in a person's own hands, which goes against how the previous steps sorted them.

keyTerms.meaning: except for
a crooked path

phrases.english: And are cold and heat at the hands of Heaven?
But it is taught: Everything is in the hands of Heaven
except for cold and heat,
as it says: 'Cold and heat are on the path of the crooked;
he who guards his soul will stay far from them'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצִינִּים פַּחִים בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם נִינְהוּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the way step 10 sorted the dangers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that cold and heat are harm from Heaven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says cold and heat are the one exception to 'everything is from Heaven,' since people can avoid them.

steps.title: Are lions and thieves really from people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second question: are lions and thieves really harm from people? רב יוסף and a ברייתא of רבי חייא say the four death penalties did not stop even after the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, are a lion and thieves really from people? But רב יוסף said, and רבי חייא taught the same: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, even though the סנהדרין stopped, the four death penalties did not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the other half of step 10's sorting, that lions and thieves count as harm from people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching that the four death penalties still go on, even without a סנהדרין, hints that Heaven brings them through other means. That could include a lion or thieves, which would make them harm from Heaven, not from people.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore
the high court that could give death penalties
the four death penalties of בית דין
stopped; were cancelled

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ אַרְיָא וְגַנָּבֵי בִּידֵי אָדָם נִינְהוּ?
phrases.english: And furthermore, are a lion and thieves at the hands of people?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: But Rav Yosef said, and Rabbi Chiya taught the same:
From the day the Temple was destroyed,
even though the Sanhedrin stopped,
the four death penalties did not stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ אַרְיָא וְגַנָּבֵי בִּידֵי אָדָם נִינְהוּ? וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second question to the one in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that lions and thieves are harm from people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the death penalties still happen through Heaven today, dangers like lions may be Heaven's way of carrying them out.

steps.title: How can the death penalties not have stopped?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the teaching can say the death penalties did not stop, when clearly they did. It then begins to explain with 'אלא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not stop?! They clearly did stop! Rather:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask about the wording of רב יוסף's teaching, and then starts to explain it. The explanation itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today there is no סנהדרין, so nobody is put to death by a court. The word 'אלא' signals that the גמרא will reread the teaching to mean that the punishment of each death penalty still happens in a different way.
